# internal/plugins/resolver/testdata — fixture provenance

Per 12-QUALITY-CONSTITUTION.md Art.2 (real-counterpart verification: a wire
or format contract is specified by bytes from a real counterpart, never by
a description) and this ticket's `docs_updates`, every file under
`fixtures/` is a byte-identical copy of a real, already-landed fixture from
this repository — not a self-authored dialect.

## fixtures/example-pbd.toml

- Source: `pkg/plugin/testdata/example-pbd.toml`, git blob
  `bc010a9565b8047d0650f86f079e8f42003819bf` (recomputed with
  `git hash-object` against both files; the copy here and the original
  share that hash, which is what "byte-identical" means).
- Provenance of the original: `pkg/plugin/testdata/README.md` — a real
  `cascade.plugin/v2` manifest for the `cascade-pbd` first-party plugin,
  golden fixture of `P1-E03-W1-S05-T6`'s `TestParseManifest_Goldens` /
  `FuzzParseManifest`.
- Why this ticket needs it: it is the only first-party manifest fixture
  that declares **two** `provides.intents` entries (`plan-phase`,
  `build-ticket`) on one plugin, which
  `TestInstalledFirstLookup`/case-insensitive-match tests need.

## fixtures/example-connector.toml

- Source: `pkg/plugin/testdata/example-connector.toml`, unchanged copy, git
  blob `82f368c7f7ae6036eba349da210e5eb31db8b3ca` for both files.
- Provenance of the original: `pkg/plugin/testdata/README.md` — golden
  fixture for the `examples: connector / agent-provider / domain` catalog

- Why this ticket needs it: a second installed manifest, used to prove an

## fixtures/registry-index.json

- Source: `pkg/plugin/testdata/registry/index.json`, git blob
  `d8a18a6eb37258a7d572f954b5b562100dd065e8` for both files (recomputed
  with `git hash-object`).
- Provenance of the original: `pkg/plugin/testdata/registry/README.md` —
  a real, verifiable Ed25519-signed registry index (schema_version "1",
  two entries: `example-formatter` tags `["formatter","example"]`,
  `example-linter` tags `["linter","example","quality"]`), generated by a
  throwaway `crypto/ed25519` Go program on 2026-09-07. The matching
  public key (`ANBaHR6iUTltVXr71FiLPG2Z2+uXL+0QoyVi6ibc3Po=`, base64) is
  reproduced in `resolver_test.go` from the same constant
  `pkg/plugin/registry_client_test.go` uses (`testRegistryPublicKeyB64`),
  so this package's tests mint a genuine `*plugin.VerifiedIndex` witness
  from these bytes through `plugin.NewVerifiedIndex`, which runs the real
  production `plugin.Ed25519Verifier.VerifyIndex` — the same verification
  `RegistryClient.Fetch` runs. There is no hand-built alternative: a
  `VerifiedIndex` has no exported field and no second constructor, so a
  test cannot fabricate one.
- Why this ticket needs it: `RegistryIndexEntry` (`pkg/plugin/registry.go`)
  carries `Name`/`Description`/`Tags`, never a `provides.intents` field —
  see `FALSE PREMISE` in the ticket journal. The registry-lookup ranking
  tiers (exact / prefix / keyword) are exercised against these real
  `Tags`/`Description` values rather than an invented `provides.intents`
  shape on `RegistryIndexEntry`, which does not exist anywhere in the
  tree.

## signed-in-test index (no fixture file)

Two ranking cases cannot be expressed by the landed fixture above, because
its two entries never match one intent at *different* tiers, and neither
entry has an id that is unmatched by its own tags, name, and description:

- exact-tag-beats-tag-prefix (`TestRegistryLookupRanking_ExactBeatsPrefix`)
- id-equality-is-not-a-tier (`TestRegistryLookupRanking_IDIsNotRanked`)

`resolver_ranking_test.go`'s `signIndex` helper therefore builds an index
document for those two cases and signs it with a freshly generated
`crypto/ed25519` key, then mints the witness from it through the same
`plugin.NewVerifiedIndex`. The bytes are produced and signed exactly the
way the registry signs them (the signature covers `schema_version` plus
the raw `entries` bytes, nothing else), and verification is the real
production verifier — no fake verifier, no bypass. What is synthesized is
the *entry content*, which is what those two cases are about; the wire
format and the crypto remain the real counterpart.

## testdata/fuzz/FuzzIntentResolve/seed001

Hand-written per the Go native fuzz corpus format (`go test fuzz v1`),
matching the shape every other package-local fuzz seed in this tree uses
(e.g. `cmd/cascade/testdata/fuzz/FuzzSinceFlagParse/seed001`). It seeds one
`string` argument — the intent being resolved — since `FuzzIntentResolve`
fuzzes only the intent-string argument against a fixed, real installed set
and a fixed, real verified index built from the fixtures above (see
`fuzz_test.go`); mutating the snapshot inputs themselves would fuzz
`plugin.ParseManifest`/`Ed25519Verifier.VerifyIndex`, which already have
their own `FuzzParseManifest`/registry fuzz targets in `pkg/plugin`.
